theorem.statement: A deterministic polynomial-time function C that, for every nonterminal 3CNF F and a polynomially chosen remaining variable v, returns epsilon in {0,1} with SAT(F) iff SAT(F[v=epsilon]) exists iff P=NP, assuming ordinary polynomial simplification and terminal checking.
forward: Starting from arbitrary 3CNF F, choose a remaining variable v by any fixed polynomial rule.
Compute epsilon=C(F,v) and replace F by the simplified cofactor F[v=epsilon].
Exactness preserves SAT status at every step.
At least one variable disappears per step, so after at most n steps a variable-free terminal formula is reached.
Each chooser/simplification step is polynomial, hence total time is polynomial and 3SAT is in P; therefore P=NP.
reverse: If P=NP, decide SAT of one cofactor in polynomial time.
If F[v=0] is SAT choose 0; otherwise choose 1 when F is SAT, and choose either value when F is UNSAT.
This yields a polynomial exact safe chooser.

TRUMP_effect.meaning: A universal chooser is not a smaller intermediate lemma. Candidate-specific certified safe-choice rules remain legitimate partial exact reducers, but receive no universal promotion without complete coverage.

next_admissible_math.target: One precisely specified polynomially certified safe-choice invariant on a hard residual class, followed by proof of scope or explicit obstruction.
